question: The Sudasari Great Indian Bustard Breeding centre is in which of the following state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Sudasari Great Indian Bustard Breeding Centre is located in the state of **Rajasthan**, specifically within the Desert National Park near Jaisalmer.
 
• Rajasthan is home to the largest population of the **Great Indian Bustard**, a critically endangered bird species native to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The breeding center was established as part of the **Conservation Breeding Programme** under the **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)** to protect and increase the dwindling population of the species.
 
• The Great Indian Bustard is primarily found in arid and semi-arid grasslands, which are abundant in Rajasthan, making it the ideal location for conservation efforts.
 
• The breeding center also focuses on habitat restoration and public awareness campaigns to minimize threats like habitat destruction, poaching, and infrastructure development. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Great Indian Bustard:**

 
 
• The **Great Indian Bustard** (*Ardeotis nigriceps*) is one of the heaviest flying birds, with a height of up to **1 meter** and a weight ranging from **8–15 kilograms**.
 
• It is listed as **Critically Endangered** on the **IUCN Red List** due to habitat loss, hunting, and human disturbances.
 
• The bird is culturally significant and has been declared the **State Bird of Rajasthan**.
 
• Its population is estimated to be fewer than **150 individuals**, primarily concentrated in Rajasthan.
 
 
 
• **Desert National Park:**
 
 
• Located in the Thar Desert near Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, the **Desert National Park** spans an area of **3162 square kilometers**.
 
• It is one of the primary habitats of the Great Indian Bustard and includes **sandy dunes, rocky terrain, and salt lakes**.
 
• Several conservation programs for the Great Indian Bustard are carried out here under the guidance of the **Wildlife Institute of India** and the **Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change**.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• India launched the **Species Recovery Programme** under the **Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats**, focusing on critically endangered species like the Great Indian Bustard.
 
• The breeding center at Sudasari focuses on captive breeding, habitat restoration, and community engagement to reduce anthropogenic pressures.
 
• The government has also implemented **eco-sensitive zones** around Desert National Park to limit infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Threats to the Great Indian Bustard:**
 
 
• Major threats include **habitat loss** due to agricultural expansion, industrialization, and urbanization.
 
• Collisions with power lines in their habitat areas have been identified as a significant cause of mortality.
 
• Conservation efforts are hindered by a lack of public awareness and community participation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Habitat Restoration:** Grassland habitats are being restored to ensure the survival of the Great Indian Bustard, with efforts to reduce human disturbances like grazing and farming.
 
• **Captive Breeding Programme:** The Sudasari Breeding Centre has successfully bred and released bustards into the wild to increase their population.
 
• **Public Awareness:** The government conducts campaigns to educate local communities on the importance of conserving the Great Indian Bustard and its habitat.
 
• **International Recognition:** The Great Indian Bustard was highlighted in the **Convention on Migratory Species (CMS) COP-13**, hosted by India in **2020**, to garner global support for its conservation.
